newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gears up for slew of property sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gears up for slew of property sales.

text.p: Hong Kong property developers are gearing up for a slew of apartment sales next month and while demand is high, lofty prices and interest rate concerns should help rein in speculation, analysts said on Friday.

"Upcoming property sales will be the real litmus test. The major developers are keen to offer these projects at a premium due to the strong demand they have seen," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"We will have to see if that demand remains now that people may be a bit concerned about affordability and the expectation that borrowing costs may go up in the future."

Analysts said that after a surge of some 20 to 30 percent in residential property prices last year and another burst upwards in early January, prices were starting to test the limits of affordability in Hong Kong.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd expects to launch sales next month at its Laguna Verde development in Hung Hom, in Kowloon.
Analysts said units at the project, which is being developed with China Light & Power Co Ltd, were likely to be priced around HK$7,500 to HK$8,000 (about US$970-$1,030) a square foot.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd is offering 108 units at three residential developments in the New Territories at about HK$5,910 to HK$7,580 per square foot.

After a fairly quiet period in the property market since mid-January, analysts said they would also be watching for sales by Wheelock Properties Ltd, New World Development Co Ltd, Sino Land Co Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd due soon.
"I expect the presales to go well but I will not expect that situation to be as ebullient in three months time," said Franklin Lam, director of property research at SBC Warburg.
"Prices are too high. I see more room on the downside than on the upside (this year)," he said.
A warning this week by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that the central bank may need to raise interest rates in coming months should be taken seriously, said Lam.

Salomon Brothers property analyst Michael Green said the comments would reduce speculation. "If it were not for Greenspan's comments, I would have expected the market in March to be highly speculative," he said.

Martin Tacon, senior associate at CS First Boston, said property developers were also expected to place restrictions on property purchases by companies in favour of individuals, a measure some experimented with earlier this year.
"I think that in itself will indeed constrain the amount of speculative activity in the projects," he said.
But analysts said the fundamentals of the market remained the same -- an acute shortage of supply.
Salomon's Green said estimated outstanding approved mortgages not yet used amounted to some HK$16.9 billion.
"Liquidity has built up and March sales will attract the build up in liquidity," he said.
Green saw residential property prices rising some 10 to 12 percent this year and Tacon expected some 16 to 20 percent.
Analysts said strength in the property market showed residents were comfortable with the handover of the territory to China on midnight of June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule.
Lam said he expected the market to remain firm until about April and then saw residential market volume beginning to decline with prices ending the year lower than at the start.

"I think what is likely to happen is sales in March will be strong and steady and then we will get a 25 basis-point increase in rates which will possibly calm things down before we start again," said Green. ($1-HK$7.74)
